About

Simulation that holds up in the test cell, and in front of the client.

I'm a Structural Simulation Engineer with 4+ years of experience delivering simulation-driven design across defence, energy and high-temperature mechanical systems. My work sits where the hard physics is: contact, plasticity, creep-fatigue interaction and fluid loads mapped onto structures.

I build FE models that are verified (mesh studies, energy balance, benchmark cases) and tied to the codes and test standards a design must pass, from ASME BPVC to CAL IV qualification envelopes. I currently lead FEA for a gas-tight premium OCTG connection at IIT Bombay.

Mumbai, Maharashtra · open to R&D roles across India and remote consulting

Featured Projects

Case studies in durability, contact and multiphysics.

Results from the project reports. Click any image to enlarge.

Case Study 01 · Tata Power · IIT Bombay

High-Temperature Power Plant Superheater Header Analysis

Residual life of an outlet final superheater header under frequent load cycling (40–100% PLF) at different ramp rates. Fully coupled thermomechanical 3D FE models in Abaqus, benchmarked against published studies, to locate critical regions and combine TMF with creep damage.

  • Standards: ASME BPVC Section VIII & Section III-NH
  • Fracture-mechanics-based life prediction across operating scenarios
+15%life-prediction accuracy over legacy empirical models; supported Tata Power in extending service intervals

Case Study 02 · ONGC · IIT Bombay · Ongoing

Gas-Tight Premium Thread Connection (OCTG Casing) Optimization

Full 3D make-up of a 4½″ 11.6# P110 premium connection for India's first indigenous gas-tight OCTG design. Implicit runs stalled at a thread run-out clash (23.7 h to turn 10°); switching to explicit converged six full make-ups in ≈53 h.

  • Elastoplastic contact at the threads, metal-to-metal seal and torque shoulder
  • Verified: energy balance 0.99995, mesh-independent within 1–5%
  • Next: friction sensitivity, DoE on seal geometry, CAL IV (API RP 5C5) load envelope
15.0kN·m make-up torque at 48°
≈265MPa seal contact pressure at first torque peak

Finding: the shoulder, not the threads, sets the torque limit; seal pressure peaks ≈20–30° past hand-tight, so maximum torque must be capped, not just minimum.

Case Study 03 · DMDE, DRDO · Technocraft Industries

Defense Superstructure Shutters: 2D CFD to Structural Coupling

Hydrodynamic loads on a stainless-steel flap assembly in seawater. Because the flap has a constant cross-section, I reduced the 3D problem to a 2D planar CFD model in Fluent, which captured the drag-governing flow physics at a fraction of the 3D cost. That made it fast to compare geometry variants before committing to full structural runs.

  • 2D planar, steady, k-ω turbulence; seawater (ρ = 1025 kg/m³), Re ≈ 3.2 × 10⁶
  • Convergence tracked through residuals and drag coefficient and drag force histories, not residuals alone
  • Drag sensitivity to geometry: cross-section and corner-fillet variants
  • CFD pressure mapped onto structural FE models for static, fatigue and modal checks on ₹100 Cr+ defence tenders
+12%structural safety margin
−25%tender approval cycle time

Case Study 04 · JSW · IIT Bombay

Root Cause Failure Analysis of Heavy Freight Rail Wagons

Root cause investigation of BFNV wagon failures. Benchmarked the design against literature and standards, then ran structural simulations of stress distribution under operational cyclic loading to locate likely crack origins and frame the design proposal.

  • Stress mapping across the underframe and bolster transitions
  • Detailed design proposal and benchmark review for the client
